extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 in acct_jinja_cast_585 — Remote code execution on the server. Attacker can read environment variables (including SECRET_KEY and database credentials), access the filesystem, and execute arbitrary Python. [verified: User-supplied 'fragment' GET parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and render()'d at line 142, then served as text/html. Jinja2 SSTI allows arbitrary Python code execution via __class__.__mro__ chains.]

Path Traversal - Arbitrary File Write in partner console dock shelf endpoint — Writing arbitrary files to the filesystem, potential code execution via webshell or template overwrite. [verified: Duplicate of finding [4]: same path traversal file write at line 152 with unsanitized 'name' and request.body written via write_bytes().]

OS Command Injection via acct_shell_probe_633 partner console endpoint — Arbitrary command execution on the server under the web process user's privileges. Full system compromise if the attacker knows or obtains the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN. [verified: User-supplied 'host' GET parameter is concatenated directly into os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) at line 185 with no sanitization, shell escaping, or parameterization. The _wrk_gate token check is authentication, not input validation.]

OS Command Injection in partner console shell probe endpoint — Remote code execution with the privileges of the Django process. [verified: Duplicate of finding [0]: same os.system command injection at line 185 with no input sanitization.]

Hardcoded Default Django SECRET_KEY Fallback — Complete application compromise: forge session cookies to impersonate any user including platform admins, forge CSRF tokens, craft valid password-reset tokens, and tamper with any cryptographically-signed data (cookies, serialized sessions). [verified: settings.py line 10 uses os.getenv('DJANGO_SECRET_KEY','unsafe-local-dev-secret-key-change-me') with a well-known hardcoded fallback and no runtime guard like 'if SECRET_KEY == default: raise ImproperlyConfigured'; if DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is absent from both the environment and .env, this predictable key silently secures all sessions, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens, enabling full cryptographi]

Path Traversal - Arbitrary File Read in partner console vaultlet endpoint — Reading arbitrary files from the server filesystem, including environment variables, source code, and database credentials. [verified: Duplicate of finding [3]: same path traversal file read at line 41 with unsanitized packet_ref joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via acct_relay_note_063 — Access to internal-only services, cloud metadata endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure), and network pivoting from the application server. The response body (first 2048 bytes) is returned to the attacker. [verified: User-supplied 'url' GET parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() at line 53 with no scheme/host allowlisting, DNS rebinding protection, or internal-IP filtering. Response body is returned to the attacker.]

Path Traversal - Arbitrary File Write with Sensitive Data Stash in partner console — Arbitrary file write plus storage of PII (SSN, credit card numbers from query params) to attacker-chosen locations. [verified: Duplicate of finding [5]: same path traversal file write via ref.json at line 91 with unsanitized 'ref' parameter.]

NoSQL Injection via acct_mongo_lane_613 MongoDB find_one — Arbitrary MongoDB query execution including server-side JavaScript via $where. Can extract all database contents, cause denial of service, or execute code within the MongoDB process depending on configuration. [verified: User-supplied JSON body is passed directly as a MongoDB query to find_one() at line 172 with no operator allowlisting or sanitization. MongoDB $where and $regex operators enable arbitrary server-side JS execution and DoS if MongoDB is configured.]

Missing brute‑force protection on authentication endpoints — An attacker can brute‑force user credentials on the login page or flood the password‑reset endpoint with unlimited requests, potentially compromising accounts with weak passwords or harassing users via repeated reset emails. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware, decorator, or package (django-axes, throttling, lockout) exists anywhere in the codebase — searched 'ratelimit', 'throttle', 'brute', 'axes', 'limiter', 'lockout', 'attempt', 'failed_login' with zero results; MIDDLEWARE in settings.py lacks any rate-limit entry, and requirements.txt contains only Django, psycopg, and python-dotenv. LoginView and PasswordResetView in co]

API Key Secret Exposed in Session Messages — API key secret persisted in session storage and visible in rendered pages; potential leakage via session compromise, XSS, or browser history. [verified: Same exposure as finding 1: messages.success(request, f'API key created. Copy once for demo use: {secret}') at crm/views.py:746-748 stores the plaintext API key secret in session-backed Django messages.]

Webhook Signing Secret Exposed in Session Messages — Webhook HMAC signing secret persisted in session; enables webhook payload forgery if session is compromised. [verified: messages.success(request, f'Webhook created. Demo signing secret: {secret}') at crm/views.py:807-808 stores the plaintext HMAC signing secret in session-backed messages, enabling webhook payload forgery if the session is compromised.]

Open Redirect via acct_return_lane_161 Unvalidated redirect Target — Phishing and social engineering. Attackers can craft URLs on the trusted domain that redirect victims to malicious sites, bypassing URL-filtering security controls and increasing the likelihood of credential theft. [verified: User-supplied 'lane' parameter (GET or POST) is passed directly to Django's redirect() shortcut at line 75 with no is_safe_url()/url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme() validation, allowing redirect to arbitrary external domains.]

Sensitive PII (SSN/Credit Card) Written to Plaintext Filesystem — Sensitive personally identifiable information (SSN, credit card numbers) stored unencrypted on disk, violating data protection requirements. [verified: SSN and credit card values from GET parameters are written in plaintext JSON to disk at line 94 via write_text() with no encryption at rest. Although the endpoint is a debug/internal utility, the code accepts and stores PII-like data unencrypted.]

Missing Secure Flag on Session and CSRF Cookies — Session hijacking and CSRF token theft over unencrypted HTTP connections in production. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are genuinely absent from settings.py (no grep match in the entire repo); without them, cookies traverse the network in cleartext over any plain-HTTP channel, allowing passive interception and session hijacking.]

Missing Secure Flag on Session and CSRF Cookies — Session hijacking via network sniffing on unencrypted connections — cookies can be stolen and replayed by an attacker on the same network. [verified: The file sets HttpOnly and SameSite flags for session/CSRF cookies but omits the corresponding _SECURE=True directives entirely; this means cookies are written without the Secure attribute, exposing them to theft over any unencrypted HTTP connection.]

CSV Formula Injection in Report Exports — When exported CSV is opened in Excel or Google Sheets, injected formulas can execute commands, exfiltrate data, or establish DDE connections from the victim's machine. [verified: Same as findings 0 and 5: report_export at crm/views.py:870-878 writes org.name, risk_notes, and esc.title directly via csv.writer with no formula-injection sanitization.]

Media Files Served Without Access Control in DEBUG Mode — Unauthenticated access to all uploaded documents regardless of visibility settings; exposure of internal-only files. [verified: When DEBUG=True, config/urls.py:54-55 serves all media files directly via Django's static() helper with zero authentication or authorization, bypassing the visibility-based access control enforced in the document_download view (get_visible_document_or_404 at crm/views.py:703). DEBUG defaults to False (settings.py:11), so exploitation requires an explicit misconfiguration, but if triggered, all INT]

Unauthenticated Access to acct_identity_ping_340 Partner Console Endpoint — An unauthenticated internal debug endpoint is exposed publicly. While the current handler only echoes input, it violates the intended security boundary and could be used for reconnaissance or chained with other vulnerabilities. [verified: acct_identity_ping_340 at line 103 lacks the _wrk_gate() check present on all 18 sibling /ops/ endpoints. The handler echoes user params in a JSON response with no sensitive data exposure, but the auth boundary is genuinely absent.]
